nodes.line: Give me a second. Right. Go.

This is going to sound small. The Benaud Oval order has been two cartons light every week since the week of the show and the invoice says otherwise every time. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Do not make a scene about it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. They admitted it, which I did not expect, so now there is $94 owing to Benaud Oval and it is not going to walk in here itself. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

npcs.name: Natasa, delivery driver at Benaud Oval

nodes.line: You are not from around the corner, are you.

Do not laugh. I do the Benaud Oval run at first light and there is a stretch of it where the van gets followed, which I have told nobody until now. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. I have got a folding table in the back of the van and the Benaud Oval shop is shut, and the number on the door rings out. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: The Benaud Oval Run — that's done.
Locked Out, Benaud Oval — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Rahel, the kid on the register at Benaud Oval

nodes.line: Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

Two people have already said no. Three of the Benaud Oval regulars have started coming in together and going out separately, and the till is $70 down on those days. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Everything Benaud Oval sells comes off a floor at Prince Alfred Square, and the woman who runs it will tell you things she will not put in writing. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do not let them talk you into anything.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: The Regulars, Benaud Oval — that's done.
The Wholesaler, Benaud Oval — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.
Fair enough. You know where I am.
Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.
Do not laugh. The canteen at Miranda does two hundred sausages on a Saturday and this week the freezer went off at half six. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Somebody walked off with the float from the Miranda canteen at about half six during the last home game, and I have a fair idea which somebody. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

Before you start: did anyone see you.
No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

This is going to sound small. Somebody has been tipping fill into the creek behind Lapstone since Thursdays and it is narrowing the channel a metre at a time. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Do not make a scene about it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. They have agreed to a clean-up at Lapstone, which is wonderful, except the grant is $127 short and closes on Thursdays. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

Do not laugh. We had 36 sandbags in the Lapstone shed on Thursdays and this morning we have got the pallet they came on. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. People keep driving the low crossing at Lapstone at quarter to six with the water over the sign, and one of them is going to be the one. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

npcs.name: Asha, resident who got flooded at Lapstone

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

Two people have already said no. The water came through my place at Lapstone on Thursdays and the assessor wants photographs of things I have already thrown out. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Whatever is happening to Lapstone starts upstream at Glenbrook, and there are people up there who have been saying so for years. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do not let them talk you into anything.
I had a feeling. Go on.
